# Stylistic Text Generator Comparator

[![Built with askThili](https://ask.thili.ai/api/v1/public/projects/zxcvtrmwsn/badge.svg)](https://ask.thili.ai/b/zxcvtrmwsn)

This project provides sports journalists with a tool to compare text generated by different language models. It showcases the power of LoRA-adapted LLMs fine-tuned on specific sports commentary styles against traditional N-gram models, offering insights into their respective text generation capabilities.

## What you are building

**Goal.** Students will build a tool that compares text generated by a LoRA-adapted LLM with an N-gram model, both fine-tuned on sports commentary, demonstrating their ability to fine-tune models and evaluate text generation quality.

**Done when.** The student has successfully fine-tuned a pre-trained LLM with a LoRA adapter on a custom sports commentary text style and implemented an N-gram model from the same text. They will have a working interface that displays and allows qualitative comparison of text generated by both models.

## Milestones

Tick these off as you go, and commit after each one.

- [ ] **1. Prepare a small corpus of sports commentary text.**  
      Hint: Focus on text cleaning and tokenization.
- [ ] **2. Implement the n-gram model and generate text from it.**  
      Hint: Apply techniques from the `Next-Word Predictor` drill.
- [ ] **3. Load a small pre-trained LLM and implement LoRA adapter injection.**  
      Hint: Use the `Build LoRA from Scratch` drill for adapter injection.
- [ ] **4. Fine-tune the LoRA adapter on the sports commentary corpus.**  
      Hint: Follow the training process from the `Build LoRA from Scratch` drill.
- [ ] **5. Generate text from the LoRA-adapted LLM.**  
      Hint: Utilize the fine-tuned LoRA model for text generation.
- [ ] **6. Provide a qualitative comparison interface for generated texts from both models.**  
      Hint: Design a simple interface to display and compare model outputs side-by-side.

## Run it

You need Python 3.12 and git.

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env        # then choose a model; see the comments inside
python -m app.cli hello
pytest
```

Your work goes in `app/core.py` (one stub per milestone) and `tests/test_core.py`. The first tests pass already; they
check the plumbing.

## Settings and secrets

Model settings live in `.env`, which is ignored by git. **Never commit `.env` or paste a key into code.** If a key ever
reaches GitHub, treat it as leaked and make a new one.

## Stretch ideas

- Allow users to adjust generation parameters (e.g., temperature, top-k) for both models.
- Enhance the comparison interface to allow users to rate or provide qualitative feedback on the generated texts.
- Implement basic visualization of text characteristics (e.g., word frequency) to aid comparison.
